title: Protocol for Isolation of Viable Adult Rat Cardiomyocytes with High Yield
protocol: Pre-warm and oxygenate the perfusion solutions.
Soak the Langendorff apparatus in 75% ethanol for 1–2 h before isolation.
Sterilize the system with 25% bleach for at least 12 hours for the first use.
Switch on the water bath to warm up the water bath-jacketed tubes of the Langendorff system.
Rinse the system 3 times with sterilized ddH2O, emptying it after each wash.
Fill Ca²⁺ KHB (∼80 mL) and Ca²⁺-free KHB (∼80 mL) into their containers.
Turn on the oxygen to oxygenate all solutions for perfusion.
Prepare heparin sodium solution and sodium pentobarbital solution.
Soak surgical tools in 75% ethanol.
Fill a 60 mm petri dish with Ca²⁺ KHB and place it on ice.
Aspirate 3–4 mL of Ca2+ KHB into a 5 mL syringe.
Connect the syringe to the cannula carefully.
Fix the syringe on an iron stand and adjust its height so that the end of the cannula is inside the petri dish.
Tie a surgical silk at the connecting site of the syringe for securing purposes.
Hold 50 mL of Ca2+ KHB in a small beaker on ice.
Cannulate the heart while it is on ice to minimize heart activity.
Inject sodium heparin intraperitoneally into the rat (200–350 g) at 1000 U/kg to prevent blood coagulation.
After 10 min, anesthetize the rat with sodium pentobarbital intraperitoneally injected at 80 mg/kg.
When the rat is in deep sleep (∼5 min after injection and no response to toe pinch), spray chest and upper abdomen with 75 % ethanol.
Make a large incision on chest well, cut through ribs on both sides to fully expose heart and lung.
Quickly remove the heart with the thymus and intact aortic arch.
Carefully remove other tissues and clean up the aortic root (leave 3–5 mm long of the aorta) with forceps and scissors.
Cannulate the heart with the cannula.
Ligate twice with the prepared surgical silk to ensure no solution leaks from the ligating site.
Cannulate the heart quickly to ensure quality cardiomyocyte isolation.
Do not insert the cannula too deeply into the aorta.
Perfuse Ca2+ KHB slowly into the aorta to exclude blood from the coronary artery and heart cavity.
Hang the heart on the Langendorff apparatus quickly after removal.
Ensure the total time from heart removal to mounting on the Langendorff system is less than 10 minutes, preferably within 5 minutes.
Connect the cannula with the heart carefully to the Langendorff system to avoid air bubbles.
Perfuse Ca2+ KHB for 5 minutes at a high flow rate of 1–2 drops per second.
Switch to perfuse Ca2+-free KHB for 4–5 min at the high flow rate.
Add 20 mL of 4× Rat Collagenase Buffer to the remaining Ca2+-Free KHB container to create 80 mL of 1× collagenase buffer.
Set a 40 min timer.
Place the heart in a small beaker (50 mL).
Set up a tube to recirculate collagenase buffer using a peristaltic pump at approximately 180 mL/min.
Add 80 μl CaCl2 (100 mM stock) into the beaker twice at 0.5–1 min intervals.
Monitor heart digestion after the heart becomes swollen and white.
Stop perfusion if collagenase solution drops increase to 180–200 drops/min.
Take off the perfused heart and remove atrium and aorta.
Put ventricular tissues in a small beaker with 10-15 mL enzyme solution (0.05% Trypsin-EDTA).
Tear the ventricular tissue into small pieces using two fine-tip forceps.
Pipette the tissue gently with a 1 ml pipette (cut tip) and place it in an incubator at 37°C for 5 min.
After 5 minutes, pipette the tissue again to check digest efficiency and cell viability under a microscope.
Stop the digestion if more than 80% rod-shaped cells are present individually.
Allow the tissues to settle by gravity for 1 minute.
Collect the supernatant from the beaker and transfer to two or three 15 mL conical tubes, each containing 5 mL of supernatant.
Add 5 mL Stop Buffer to each tube and pipette up and down 3 times to mix.
Add 10–15 mL 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA solution to the left precipitated cardiac tissue in the beaker.
Repeat steps for trypsin digestion (Figure 4C).
Collect the sediment of cardiomyocytes through gravity, pipette up and down to mix and wait for 3–4 minutes (Figure 4D).
Repeat digestion with trypsin 1–2 times if necessary to obtain more myocytes.
Sequentially add 25 μl CaCl2 (100 mM stock) to cells in the conical tubes three times at 5-minute intervals, mix well each time.
Add 50 μl CaCl2 and mix well for the fourth addition.
Collect the precipitated live cardiomyocytes through 30 g, 30 s centrifugation and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells with 2 mL culture medium.
Merge all cells into one tube.
Replenish the culture medium to 10 mL and mix well.
Pre-coat the 6 well plates or dishes with 40 μg/mL laminin (1 mL per well) for 30 min before cardiomyocyte purification.
Count the cell number.
Plate cells with 500 μl culture medium per well at a density of 5 × 10^4 cells/mL.
Incubate the plate at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Gently change the medium with 2 mL fresh culture medium two hours later for continued culture.
